findings.detail: Official Eponet wiki states QR opens a browser flow whose step 1 exposes current station price and price details; operator controls start/kWh/blocking/parking fees.
Official portal documentation shows each QR is associated with Charger ID + EVSE ID; example Charger ID 25-5889 / EVSE CHEPOE0001749; downloaded filename QR-Code_CH-EPO-E0001749.svg.
Official screenshots show the QR/ad-hoc flow runs on portal.eponet.ch.
Official wiki currently links to https://www.eponet.info/adhoc_laden; current fetchers cannot reach this host/path.
Eight Charger IDs are embedded in current national inventory names, covering 23 EVSE; see switzerland-epo-charger-id-pivot-2026-09-29.json.
adhoccharging.eu currently indexes 72 Eponet stations / 338 charge points but exposes no Eponet direct prices for tested known Charger-ID sites; useful for inventory/status, not tariff resolution.
Guessed portal routes /adhoc_laden, /adhoc_laden.php, /adhoc, /publiccharge.php, /public_charging.php and /charge.php return 404; QR target likely uses a different path or tokenized/query route.
Search engines did not index portal.eponet.ch price/ad-hoc pages or exact known Charger-ID/EVSE QR targets.
Connected Firecrawl account has insufficient credits; no Firecrawl-based source inspection possible now.
Official Eponet QR for Charger ID 23-2116 / EVSE CH*EPO*E0001579 decodes to https://portal.eponet.ch/public-charge.php?id=243fdf344f5a44f4872998649ca89eb3.
Public charge uses an opaque 32-hex id token rather than exposing Charger ID/EVSE ID directly in the URL.

Read-only fetch of that QR target returns Charging Port UI with Start Price 0.00 CHF and Price/kWh 0.00 CHF plus Immoconnect/Public Charging choice. This sample EVSE is not present in the current repo EPO snapshot and is retained only as a technical fixture, not tariff evidence for current 324 EVSE.
Simple MD5/SHA1/SHA256 candidates built from Charger ID 23-2116 and EVSE CH*EPO*E0001579 do not reproduce token 243fdf344f5a44f4872998649ca89eb3; token should be treated as backend-generated/opaque.
Three official public-charging tutorial photos were tested through QR decoding but did not yield additional decodable QR targets at available resolution.

nextSafeTests: Recover one or more public-charge tokens belonging to EVSEs in the current 324-EVSE snapshot, ideally by finding published charger-label photos/QR images for known stations.
Static-inspect Eponet Go APK/XAPK when the attachment is accessible; search for public-charge.php, QR scanner handling, charger lookup/API endpoints and token fields.
Search public station/operator websites and image indexes using exact current EVSE IDs + Charger IDs to locate photographed Eponet labels.
Once one current-snapshot token is found, validate that public-charge page against station identity and tariff, then scale only through exact token evidence.
policy: No brute-force enumeration, no charging/payment action, no tariff extrapolation. Only public read-only endpoints and exact identity matches.
